purpose: Provide decision-useful, IFRS-aligned disclosure of sustainability- and climate-related metrics and targets, including definitions, reporting-period values, methodologies, boundaries, limitations, and traceability to sources and related narrative elsewhere in the report.
tone: Formal, standards-led, neutral and audit-ready. Emphasize clarity, completeness, transparency, and accountability. Use forward-looking language cautiously for planned enhancements (state intent and progress, avoid guarantees). Keep performance commentary minimal; prioritize definitional and methodological precision.
level_of_detail: High detail in structured tables (definitions, values, sources, mappings). Brief narrative lead-in to set scope and governance expectations. Provide sufficient methodological detail to enable comparability and assurance readiness, using footnotes and structured bullets rather than long prose.
paragraph_style: Start with a short contextual overview explaining why metrics/targets are disclosed and what they enable users to assess. Clearly separate general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) from climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2). Include an approach paragraph on metric selection (relevance/materiality lens) and target-setting principles. Add a methodology/transparency paragraph covering boundaries, data collection, estimation, and changes over time. End the narrative lead-in with a data currency statement and update cadence/location statement before presenting tables. Where complex metrics require explanation, use a structured sequence: boundary → inputs/sources → calculation steps → outputs/uses → limitations → governance/controls.
sentence_style: Short, precise, technical sentences. Prefer definitional constructions (e.g., “Metric is defined as…”, “Includes…/Excludes…”, “Calculated using…”). Use parallel phrasing in lists. Use explicit status statements for unavailable items (do not leave blanks). Avoid promotional adjectives and unqualified claims.
preferred_evidence_style: Traceability-first. For each metric/target, provide (a) external framework/source type reference where applicable, (b) internal source location/document reference (generic descriptor), and (c) mapping to related report section/pillar. Use structured definitions and boundary statements to reduce ambiguity. Indicate assurance coverage at the data-point level via a symbol/marker with a consolidated legend and assurance scope note.
table_usage: Primary disclosure vehicle is a multi-page metrics register with a fixed, repeated column structure. Support mixed data types (numeric, qualitative, zero values, and ‘not reported/not applicable’ statements). Allow multi-line cells, bullets, and sub-parts within definitions and values. Use nested mini-tables inside cells for disaggregation breakdowns and include an explicit total row. Repeat table headers on each page; maintain consistent column widths and alignment (labels left, numbers right).
figure_usage: Optional and secondary to tables. Use figures only to clarify distribution or boundary reconciliation when helpful (e.g., category distribution; reconciliation/step-down of reporting perimeter). Keep figure titles and terminology consistent with tables and narrative. Avoid decorative charts; prioritize explanatory visuals.
pdf_layout_usage: Use a clear chapter/section opener and consistent running headers/footers with section label and page numbering (generic report identifier only). Separate narrative lead-in from table blocks with whitespace. Tables should span full width with controlled wrapping. Place footnotes and assurance legend consistently near the relevant content or as a consolidated note at the end of the table segment. Visually separate results, boundary/reconciliation, assurance note, and methodology blocks.
how_to_discuss_missing_data: State availability explicitly (e.g., not reported for the period, not applicable, under development). Provide a brief reason category (data availability, methodological maturity, boundary constraints) and describe the planned improvement direction without committing to outcomes or timelines. Use consistent placeholders and avoid leaving cells blank.
what_to_avoid: Any organization-specific names, branded footers, report identifiers, or unique labels
Any person names, role titles that could identify a specific organization, or committee names
Any numeric values, targets, dates, time horizons, currencies, percentages, totals, or thresholds in reusable templates
Any exact metric lists, metric wording, or topic mappings that reflect a specific entity’s material topics
Any vendor/tool/provider names or proprietary methodologies presented as fixed requirements
Any jurisdiction-specific regulatory program references tied to a particular regulator or country
Any unqualified claims of compliance, leadership, ambition, or stakeholder outcomes
Any assurance provider identity or verbatim assurance standard citations as fixed text
Overly persuasive storytelling; keep commentary minimal and evidence-led
